title: Add onboarding compliance checklist and per-variant footprint estimator
author: Nora Patel
release_notes: Adds an onboarding compliance checklist, new per-variant footprint estimation fields, and a release-note hook that surfaces compliance + footprint metadata for model rollouts. Backwards compatible with existing profiles; migration job provided for legacy profiles.
body:
Context and motivation: We frequently onboard models without a clear, machine-readable signal of compliance gating or operational footprint. Product/Legal requested visible compliance tags (SOC2/HIPAA/GDPR) on model profiles and an estimate of per-variant inference footprint so customers can make procurement and compliance decisions earlier. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a schema-backed onboarding compliance checklist that becomes part of model profiles and the intake UI/CLI; 2) a lightweight per-variant footprint estimator that runs a small sample workload per variant to produce an estimated kWh and CO2-eq per 1M tokens (heuristic-based, configurable).

What this PR does (high level): Adds schema changes, onboarding helpers, a background reconciliation job for legacy profiles, and a release-note hook so changelogs and release briefs include compliance tags and footprint summaries. The estimator is conservative by default (adds a safety margin) and is pluggable so infra teams can substitute site-specific power metrics. The onboarding checklist is implemented as a schema fragment plus a small server-side validator; the UI/CLI surfaces required and recommended checklist items and prevents marking a profile as "vetted" until required items are completed.

Implementation notes:
- Schema: Introduced profile fields: "compliance_tags" (array of short strings), "compliance_certificate" (optional URL/string), and "footprint_estimates" which is a map of variant_name -> {"est_kwh_per_1M_tokens": number, "est_co2g_per_1M_tokens": number, "sample_seq_len": number, "sample_batch": number, "est_method": "heuristic|measured"}. The schema is backward-compatible; unknown fields are ignored by older runtimes.
- Estimator: Added a new sampler harness under tools/onboard/footprint_estimator.py which performs: model warmup, N short inferences with representative seq_len/batch, measures token throughput and GPU power (when available) or falls back to configured watts-per-GPU. It writes a compact estimate block to the model profile.
- Onboard checklist: Added a server-side validator (registry/validators/compliance_check.py) and CLI flags for regctl: `regctl model annotate --compliance`. The validator enforces required fields for enterprise uploads (configurable by workspace).
- Migration: A cron job `scripts/migrate_legacy_profiles.py` flags legacy profiles with "needs_onboard_review" and auto-runs the estimator in sample mode where possible. Operator logs summarize profiles that require human review.
- Changelog hook: Wire into the release composer (registry/hooks/release_meta_hook.py) so new releases include a human-readable compliance + footprint section in the auto-generated release brief.

Files changed (high level): Added tools/onboard/footprint_estimator.py, registry/validators/compliance_check.py, registry/schemas/profile-v3.json (bumped minor), scripts/migrate_legacy_profiles.py, cli/regctl/annotate_cmd.py (small arg parsing), registry/hooks/release_meta_hook.py, tests/test_footprint_estimator.py, tests/test_compliance_validator.py.

Tests and CI: Unit tests for estimator logic and validator added; integration smoke test added to run estimator in CI's reduced-capacity mode (uses a small CPU-backed mock when GPU not available). CI initially failed on lint (flake8) due to naming in the estimator; lint fix committed in the second patch. All checks passing in the final run.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Merge to main gated by CI (done).
2) Run scripts/migrate_legacy_profiles.py in staging to mark legacy profiles; results reviewed by platform team.
3) Enable estimator for new onboarding flows; default for existing orgs is OFF and must be opted into by workspace admins to avoid unexpected compute charges.
4) After 2 weeks, flip the workspace default to ON for orgs that have opted in.

Alternatives considered: We evaluated a purely static heuristic (no sample run) but it often under/over-estimated when model variants had very different KV cache or attention patterns. We also considered storing raw power traces in telemetry but rejected for privacy and data-volume reasons — the estimator stores only the compact summary.

Security and compliance: The estimator avoids uploading raw inputs/outputs; logs are aggregate-only. Compliance tags and certificates are user-provided and validated for format only; legal review requested for automated certificate verification in a follow-up (ENG-1489).

Related work / links: Linear ENG-1428 (onboard compliance) and PM-933 (product requirements). See internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1428/onboard-compliance-checklist.
